title: A finished task no longer starts a Periodical by default; Periodicals run when chosen
description:
## As asked

**Repository:** JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour).

**What this is for.** When a run scoped to one task merges it, the run then starts one Periodical, if any is due or has had work merged in its repo since it last ran. There are 15 Periodicals that read a repo, so that is nearly always, and each task brought one. On 10 Nov these came to about $101, a quarter of the day's spend, and none changed code. John: "we probably don't need a periodical every time by default?" and "I very much agree."

**What we want.** A finished task doesn't start a Periodical unless it was asked to. Periodicals still run when chosen: by a person, or by a goal that asks for one. A general run's own order of work is unchanged.

**Done when** a task that merges without being asked for a Periodical starts none, and a Periodical can still be started on purpose.

**Every change names what it retires. Questions:** settle engineering questions yourself; only John's calls (product, money, authority, what to retire) go to him as rulings.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Size of the move

**Size:** just the task
**Why:** A scoped run stops once its task is done and starts a Periodical only when asked, retiring the completion Periodical and its chain guard; no Survey finding binds beyond that, so a weekly-floor driver and reading cost stay out.
**Cuts:** none
**Decided by:** the standing policy

## Implementation Plan

Implemented as approved in [PR #2396](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2396>), merged as `b5950f704` and deployed on 11 Nov 2026. It had two declared minor departures, both accepted by review. The scoped line extends the existing "Do not pull other tasks off the stack" sentence. Witness 4 uses plan-review's three-change expectation.

Session fit: fits one session.

plan-review due: yes

## Outcome

A scoped Autopilot run now stops once its task is merged and verified. It starts a Periodical only when the human's goal asks for one. Mint routes and UI are unchanged, and general-run ranks are byte-identical.

Retired, as named in the PR: the completion tail and its two kickoff pointers; its chain guard (`periodicalReview`); LIN-4349's budget branch; and the tail as the incidental weekly-floor driver (John ruled retire-floor).

Post-deploy, still open for the operator: the first hand-started Mint + Autopilot should produce no second mint. Monitor and rollback are in the close-out comment.

The full plan, research and revisions are preserved in the task snapshots and the comment trail.

## Survey open-0: LIN-4415 @ da5df707d

**Where it lives.** In a prompt, not in code. `AUTOPILOT_PRECEDENCE` (`lib/prompts/autopilot-precedence.js`) has the paragraph "The tail: a scoped run ends with one Periodical", and the scoped goal line at `lib/prompts/autopilot-kickoff.js:737` says "take the policy's tail". No server code mints. The run reads `GET /periodicals` and mints the lane itself. The change is mostly deleting text.

**Why it's harder than it looks**

1. **It reverses a ruling from three days ago, and quietly retires the weekly floor.** The tail arrived on 8 Nov (LIN-4382), and LIN-4349 (783349ae7) refined it as "the ruled 'one Periodical run, two sessions'". John's quotes cover reversing it. But the tail was the one dependable thing serving rank 2 ("a lane reading `due`, the weekly floor"), because it took `due`/`never` before `landed`. Without it, a `due` lane runs only when a *general* run starts or someone mints one by hand. If most runs are scoped, Periodicals may simply stop. That's a money/product question: a ruling for John, and named in the PR as retired.
2. **Machinery that exists only for the tail.** That's `periodicalReview` on `buildAutopilotKickoff`, `periodicalReviewNote`, `lib/dispatch-entrance.js:1858` (gate marker → kickoff) and the "takes no tail" sentences. With no default tail there's no chain to guard, so retire them. Keep `resolvePeriodicalIdFromGateMarker` itself (used at `dispatch-entrance.js:1582` and in `routes/proxy.js`).
3. **Heavy pinning.** `tests/unit/autopilot-kickoff.test.js` has about 41 hits, including LIN-4349's pins of both budget branches. `lin-4382-precedence-written-once.test.js` has about 34. Also affected: `workspace-api-autopilot-variant`, `lin-4375-session-pr-wins`, the scoped golden fixture, `docs/autopilot-operating-manual.md:526`, `docs/autopilot-kickoff.md` and the catalogue's kickoff line. The written-once test fails if the ranks are restated, so "if asked" can't become a second copy of the order inside the kickoff.
4. **What counts as "asked".** Starting one on purpose already works: `POST /periodicals/{id}/mint`, with or without `autopilot: true`. A scoped run's goal has no structured field. It rides along as "Additional context from the human" (LIN-2818). Rank 1 plus the rank 2/4 mint-and-drive text already tell a run how to act on a goal that asks for a Periodical. Treat the goal text as the opt-in and add no new flag. That's an engineering call, not John's.

**Symptom or cause?** Partly a symptom. With 15 repo-scoped lanes, `landed` after one day (`LANDED_MIN_GAP_MS`) and `never` counting as most overdue, almost every tail found a lane. The bigger lever on the $101 is the cost of each reading, which is out of scope here.

**What I'd do first**

- Ask John before editing: is it OK for `due` lanes to run only from general runs and manual mints, or should something else (e.g. a scheduled general run) serve the floor?
- Then make one prompt change: drop the tail paragraph, and make the scoped line "stop when it is done; take a Periodical only if the human's goal asks for one (as at rank 2 or 4)". Retire the `periodicalReview` path. Re-capture the golden on purpose, and replace the budget-branch pins with one pin: a scoped prompt mentions no Periodical unless its goal does.

## Survey global: LIN-4415 @ da5df707d

**Where it lands.** Nothing on the server mints a Periodical after a merge. The behaviour is one paragraph of prompt text, "The tail: a scoped run ends with one Periodical", in `AUTOPILOT_PRECEDENCE` (`lib/prompts/autopilot-precedence.js`). The scoped goal line at `lib/prompts/autopilot-kickoff.js:737` points at it. This code is three days old (LIN-4382, LIN-4349) and improving: the order of work now lives in one constant, guarded by `lin-4382-precedence-written-once.test.js`. The tail is the weak spot. It was patched within a day (the budget branch). Its chain guard exists twice, as prose (the gate-marker sentence) and as a `periodicalReview` line, and only `POST /autopilot/kickoff` sets that line (`dispatch-entrance.js:1858`). The copy-prompt kickoffs in `routes/workspace-api-prompts.js` rely on the prose alone.

**The obvious way.** Delete the tail paragraph and make the scoped line say "once it is complete, stop". That retires:
- `periodicalReview` and `periodicalReviewNote` in the kickoff
- the gate-marker step at `dispatch-entrance.js:1858`
- the tail's tests in the written-once and `autopilot-kickoff` suites, and the scoped golden (recapture it on purpose)

Keep `resolvePeriodicalIdFromGateMarker` (still used at `dispatch-entrance.js:1582` and `routes/proxy.js:1483/1557`). Keep `scope` on `GET /periodicals` (rank 2's `never` rule reads it), but fix its comments at `routes/proxy-compute.js:1063` and `lib/periodical-runs.js:437`, which cite the tail.

What would notice: the tests pin the tail's text, so they fail loudly. The docs would not. The test only checks that docs name the constant, so stale tail sentences would survive in `docs/autopilot.md:174-176`, `docs/autopilot-kickoff.md` (~99-106, 170), `docs/autopilot-operating-manual.md:526`, `docs/architecture/source-map.md:183-184` and `lib/proxy-instructions.js:933`.

Watch out for the word "tail". `PERIODICAL_AUTOPILOT_TAIL` and `withAutopilotTail` in `lib/periodicals.js` are a different tail, the Mint + Autopilot handoff, and they are how a person starts a Periodical on purpose. Delete them by grep and the "still startable" half of Done breaks.

**The second copy to avoid.** Don't turn "unless asked" into a new condition inside the tail. Rank 1 ("an explicit goal from the human") already reaches a scoped run as `**Additional context from the human:**` (LIN-2818). Intentional starts already work through `POST /periodicals/{id}/mint` (plain or `autopilot: true`) and the UI's Mint / Mint + Autopilot. A conditional tail would mean two opt-in paths and keep the guard machinery alive.

**What the ticket is aimed at.** It retires more than it names. Nothing schedules `due` lanes. Rank 2, "the weekly floor", runs only when an Autopilot run reads the policy, and scoped runs were the frequent readers. So the tail was, in effect, the floor's scheduler. Without it, `due` lanes move only on general runs or a person's mint. Retiring that is John's call, and it should be ruled before the edit.

**Better, at this task's cost:** remove the tail outright, retire its guard plumbing, update all five doc sites, and add one test line that fails if a scoped kickoff mentions minting a Periodical.

**Better still, not this task's:**
- a real driver for the weekly floor (a server-side due sweep), not prompt text that runs as a side effect
- the cost per reading (~$7 on 10 Nov) and eligibility tuning

Retire it. Periodicals run only when chosen: by a person, a goal that asks, or a general run.

— Ruling recorded via Harbour

Accept: overdue lanes run only from general runs and hand-started mints; name this retirement in the PR

— Ruling recorded via Harbour

### Plan Review Verdict

**Verdict:** Approve. The plan removes the cause, which is the completion-tail prompt text and its pointers. It keeps every way of starting a Periodical on purpose, and it names what it retires.

**How it meets the ask:** "A finished task doesn't start a Periodical unless it was asked to. Periodicals still run when chosen: by a person, or by a goal that asks for one. A general run's own order of work is unchanged." No narrowing. Cuts: none.

**What I checked (main = `da5df707d`, no commits since the ticket was filed):**
- **The premise holds.** Nothing on the server mints after a merge. The only thing that does is the "**The tail: a scoped run ends with one Periodical.**" paragraph in `AUTOPILOT_PRECEDENCE`, plus its pointers at `autopilot-kickoff.js:562` and `:737`. I rendered a general and a scoped kickoff at HEAD to confirm this.
- **The chain guard is safe to retire.** `PERIODICAL_AUTOPILOT_TAIL` (`lib/periodicals.js`) kicks off `POST /autopilot/kickoff` with only `issueIdentifier` and no `goal`. So once this lands, a review's own run is a scoped run with no goal, and it stops. `periodicalReview` appears only in `dispatch-entrance.js:1856-1879`, the two prompt files and the written-once test, so removing it is clean. `resolvePeriodicalIdFromGateMarker` stays because `:1582` and `routes/proxy.js` still use it.
- **The census is complete.** I re-ran the plan's grep and widened it to `public/`, `views/` and a bare "the tail". Every Periodical-related hit outside the dated records is in the plan's table. The other "tail" hits are unrelated: CI-wake lineage, the feedback tail, CSS, and `withAutopilotTail`.
- **The written-once constraint holds.** The proposed scoped line ("no other stack task and no Periodical unless the human's goal asks") matches none of the `RANK_PATTERNS` that remain. Dropping `/a scoped run ends with one Periodical/i` still leaves `RANK_PATTERNS.slice(4)` meaningful.
- **The weekly floor needs no new ruling.** The As-asked block, in John's words, keeps Periodicals running "when chosen" and leaves a general run's order unchanged. That means rank 2 (`due`) still runs on general runs. Losing the tail as the floor's incidental driver follows directly from the ask, not from an unasked cut, and the plan names it as retirement 4. This approval depends on the PR body putting that consequence, and the server-sweep / scheduled-general-run follow-up question, in front of John.

**Notes for the builder (none block):**
1. **`docs/autopilot-operating-manual.md:526` is runtime prompt text, not only a doc.** `buildAutopilotManual()` inlines the manual into every kickoff, general included. In the rendered kickoff it is line ~540: "…has taken the precedence policy's tail (at most one Periodical…)". Edit it as prompt text. Witness 1's check over the full rendered text will catch it if it is missed.
2. **Witness 4 expects the wrong diff.** The general render will not differ by "exactly the deleted tail paragraph". Step 5's complete branch is in the shared guide, so it renders in general runs too, as does the manual line from note 1. Expect three changes in the general before/after diff: the policy paragraph, step 5's "take the policy's tail (step 1), report and stop" becoming "report and stop", and the manual sentence. What must stay byte-identical is the two rank paragraphs, and the existing rank-order test pins them.
3. **Witness 1's third bullet already passes at HEAD.** The scoped snapshot (`## Where things stand`) has no `/periodicals` read today; only the policy block and the general first act carry one. Keep it as a regression pin, but don't count it as failing at HEAD. The goal-block wording and the retired-phrase checks are the parts that fail at HEAD.
4. **Budget interaction (no action, mention in the PR).** With the LIN-4349 branch gone, a scoped run that declares `maxTasks` and whose goal asks for a Periodical will mint and then get `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` when it tries to drive the review. General budgeted runs already behave this way under rank 2/4, and real scoped runs declare no budget. A short line in the PR's retirement 3 is enough.
5. In the written-once file, also rewrite the header bullet "The tail names the gate marker… takes no tail" (lines 9-11) when the marker test goes. Witness 5's census covers `lib/`/`routes/`/docs but not `tests/`, so nothing would flag that stale text.

**Next:** `implementation`, with these notes.

## Implementation: LIN-4415

**PR:** https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2396
**Branch:** `feat/lin-4415-no-default-completion-periodical` · commit `57b04f0b2` (on `da5df707d`; main has not moved since)
**CI:** green (Unit tests, E2E 1–4/4, secret scan, `CI success`).

**What changed.** A scoped run now stops once its task is merged and verified. It starts a Periodical only when the human's goal asks for one. Starting one on purpose still works: by a person (the mint routes and UI, unchanged), by a goal (rank 1 and the mint instruction still render), or by a general run (ranks byte-identical).

**What it retires** (listed in the PR):
1. the completion tail and its two kickoff pointers;
2. its chain guard (`periodicalReview` / `periodicalReviewNote`, the gate-marker step in `POST /autopilot/kickoff`, the policy's marker sentence);
3. LIN-4349's budget branch. A budgeted scoped run whose goal asks for a Periodical may now get `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` when it drives the review. Real scoped runs declare no budget;
4. the tail as the weekly floor's de facto scheduler.

The PR puts the follow-up question to John: should a server-side due sweep or a scheduled general run serve the floor? Nothing is filed for it.

**Plan-review notes applied:**
- (1) the manual sentence was edited as runtime text;
- (2) the general before/after diff shows exactly three changes: the policy paragraph, step 5 and the manual sentence;
- (3) the `/periodicals` snapshot check is kept as a regression pin, not counted as failing at base;
- (4) the budget consequence is in the PR;
- (5) the written-once header was rewritten.

**Departures from the plan:**
- The scoped line keeps the existing "Do not pull other tasks off the stack" sentence and adds ", and start no Periodical unless the human's goal asks for one". This keeps the diff smaller and leaves two existing pins valid.
- Witness 4 uses the three-change expectation from review note 2.

**Evidence:**
- With `lib/`, `routes/` and `docs/` reverted to base, the new and changed tests produce 10 failures. They all pass with the change. The census lists every row of the plan's table at base.
- The goal opt-in tests pass both before and after (kept behaviour).
- `lin-4313`, `lin-4317` and `periodicals.test.js` are unchanged and green.
- The scoped golden diff is the goal block's last two lines only.
- Local full unit run: 24849/24850. The one failure is an environmental code-shape test (a parent folder's `node_modules/acorn`); it passed in CI.

**Not shown by tests:** production confirmation needs the mint event count on `/api/proxy/periodicals/:id/mint` and daily Periodical spend to drop.

### Leftovers

PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2396 · head `98a7e299878a98e86f12e5f89201cdc616b27a56` · CI green (Unit, E2E 1–4/4, secret scan, `CI success`).

- `docs/architecture/source-map.md`: the periodical-runs entry said `scope` serves the policy's "repo-only rules". Only the `never` rule is left, so it now says that. **tidied**
- `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md` (Lessons): added that a scoped run's Periodical is opt-in by goal, with no tail and no flag (LIN-4415). The LIN-4349 lesson stays, but I shortened it and dropped its `maxTasks: null` example to fit the note's 6,144-byte cap. **tidied (lesson)**
- `docs/areas/runs-and-dispatch.md`: the `periodicalReview` waiting entry is gone. My change made it untrue, and it was removed in the first commit. **tidied**
- Weekly-floor driver (a server-side sweep for due Periodicals, or a scheduled general run): this is outside the prompts area, and whether to build it is John's call, asked in the PR body. **for close-out**: file it only if John rules for it.

Considered, not a leftover: the policy's "To act on rank 2 or 4" sentence also serves a goal that asks for a Periodical (rank 1). Plan-review judged that sufficient, and a test pins it (goal plus rank 1 plus the mint instruction). Widening it would change a rank paragraph this change keeps byte-identical.

## Review — LIN-4415

PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2396 · reviewed head `98a7e299878a98e86f12e5f89201cdc616b27a56` (on `da5df707d`; main has since moved only by `fe2f1f0`, which touches docs this PR doesn't, so the PR is MERGEABLE).

CI: green on `98a7e29`: Unit tests, E2E 1–4/4, secret scan, `CI success`. I also ran the targeted suites locally: kickoff, written-once, periodicals route, `periodicals`, `lin-4313`, `lin-4317`. 713/713 pass.

**Staleness.** Since the ticket was filed, none of the ticket's paths changed on main. The plan's premise still holds at HEAD: nothing on the server mints after a merge, and the behaviour was the `AUTOPILOT_PRECEDENCE` paragraph plus its two kickoff pointers.

**Scope vs plan.** The diff covers every row of the plan's table and touches no other file, apart from one leftovers commit (source-map wording and an `llm-and-prompts` lesson), which the builder's `### Leftovers` comment records. The plan's two departures are minor and were declared: the scoped line extends the existing sentence, and witness 4 uses plan-review's three-change expectation. Both are fine.

**Regression check.** `git log` on the touched files: `236001232`/`783349ae7` (LIN-4382/4349) built what this change retires, and John's ruling covers that reversal. `7ac075daf` (LIN-4392) and `b369ff3bb` (LIN-4398) are intact. `isPeriodicalReview` is untouched, and `resolvePeriodicalIdFromGateMarker` is still imported and used at `dispatch-entrance.js:1582` and `routes/proxy.js:1483,1557`. Nothing that was previously reverted is re-applied.

**General order unchanged (independently re-rendered).** I diffed the general kickoff rendered at `da5df70` against the one at head. There are exactly three hunks: the manual sentence (line 541), the deleted tail paragraph (656), and step 5's complete branch (734). The rank paragraphs are byte-identical.

**Mutation checks (each reverted afterwards; tree clean):**
- M1, restore base `autopilot-precedence.js` (tail paragraph back): 5 fail, including the census, "policy names no gate marker and no tail", the route tests for review and ordinary tasks, and "carries none of the retired wording".
- M2, restore the old scoped goal line: 10 fail, including the golden, witness 1, and the census.
- M3, put the "precedence policy's tail" sentence back in `docs/autopilot-operating-manual.md`, which is inlined runtime text: the census and the rendered-text witnesses fail.
- M4, change "mint the lane with" to "open the lane with": both goal opt-in witnesses (builder and route) fail, along with the existing rank 2/4 mint pin.
- M5, inject an "is the review task of the …" line into the scoped block: the route's gate-marked review test and the golden fail.

Every new or changed load-bearing test goes red when its own claimed path is removed.

**Test level.** The behaviour is prompt text, so the right witness is the rendered prompt through the real route (`POST /api/proxy/autopilot/kickoff`), which the tests already drive with a gate-marked and an ordinary task. No e2e is needed. Whether the model actually complies is not testable here; see the ledger.

**Isolated, or one of a class?** The class is "a path that starts a Periodical nobody asked for". I searched for mint call sites (`/mint` across `lib`, `routes` and `public`) and for any prompt text tying merge to Periodical:
- The only minting paths are the deliberate ones: the mint route in `routes/proxy-dispatch.js:310` and its UI, plus general-run ranks 2 and 4. The As-asked block keeps both.
- Every scoped variant (standard and stepper, each in write and readonly) renders the new stop line.
- The copy-prompt kickoffs (`routes/workspace-api-prompts.js`, `workspace-api-feedback.js`) get the same text from the shared builder.
- The remaining "tail" hits in a scoped render (lines 402–403, 769) are unrelated: one is about session sizing, the other about settling.
- A wider grep, also covering `public/`, `views/`, `scripts/` and `tests/`, finds no stale retired wording.

The change is isolated, with no unhandled siblings.

**Leftovers.** The builder's list matches the diff, and nothing else is left at the edges. A context note, not an item: `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md` is now 6,143 bytes against its 6,144-byte cap, so the next lesson there will need a trim.

**Area notes.** I applied `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md`:
- "Never restate a rank; LIN-4382": the new scoped line restates no rank.
- LIN-4369 says prompt words that ban a behaviour don't hold it alone. That is why the production monitor below is necessary.

The `runs-and-dispatch.md` waiting entry was correctly removed, per the README rule on untrue entries.

**Rulings.** Both are answered: `lin-4415-weekly-floor` chose retire-floor, and overdue lanes run only from general runs and hand-started mints. I am raising no new decision. Since John chose "retire", close-out should **not** file the weekly-floor scheduler follow-up; the builder's leftover already makes it conditional on a ruling for it. The PR body's "For John" question can stay as information.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Inside** (the ticket's core claim: "a task that merges without being asked for a Periodical starts none"). Whether real scoped runs actually stop minting. The tests prove the prompt text, not the model's compliance (LIN-4369). Rank 2/4 text still renders in scoped runs, so a scoped run could in principle still mint from it.
  - **After the deploy, named monitor:** compare proxy events on `POST /api/proxy/periodicals/:id/mint` before and after the deploy. A mint whose dispatching session is a scoped Autopilot run with no Periodical in its goal is a failure. Expected: mints drop from about one per merged scoped task to intentional ones only, and daily Periodical spend (~$101 on 10 Nov) falls with them. Nothing short of production shows model behaviour across real runs.
  - **Named rollback:** revert PR #2396's merge commit on main. The change is prompt text and comments with no persisted data, so it is fully reversible.
- **Inside** (the "still startable on purpose" half of Done). A real Mint + Autopilot handoff after deploy: the review's own run is scoped with no goal, so it should stop after its task and not chain another mint. The route test proves the prompt this run receives.
  - **After the deploy:** on the first hand-started Mint + Autopilot, check the mint event log shows no second mint from that run.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger

How it meets the As-asked block, sentence by sentence:
- "When a run scoped to one task merges it, the run then starts one Periodical…" This is the cause, and the change removes it at the source: the policy paragraph and both kickoff pointers.
- "A finished task doesn't start a Periodical unless it was asked to." The scoped goal line now reads "start no Periodical unless the human's goal asks for one. Once it is complete, stop". Witnessed and mutation-checked.
- "Periodicals still run when chosen: by a person, or by a goal that asks for one." The mint routes and UI are unchanged (`lin-4313`/`lin-4317`/`periodicals` green). Goal opt-in is witnessed in the builder and the route.
- "A general run's own order of work is unchanged." The ranks are byte-identical (re-rendered diff above).
- "Done when…" Text: met and tested. Production: ledger item 1.
- "Every change names what it retires." The PR body names all four: the tail, the chain guard, the LIN-4349 budget branch, and the weekly-floor driver, including the budget consequence.
- "Questions…" The weekly-floor call went to John as a ruling and was answered. The engineering calls were settled in-stage.

There are no narrowings and no fixes for close-out to make. Close-out merges once CI is re-checked on the exact head, then runs the two post-deploy checks. It files no scheduler follow-up (ruled retire-floor).

## Close-out — LIN-4415

**Merged:** [PR #2396](https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2396) as merge commit `b5950f704`. It was pinned with `--match-head-commit` to the reviewed head `98a7e29`. **Deployed:** the production footer reads `b5950f7`, observed before 22:44 UTC on 11 Nov.

**CI:** green on the exact head `98a7e29` when merged (Unit tests, E2E 1–4/4, secret scan, `CI success`; run 43110345757). Main CI on `b5950f704` is also green.

**How it meets the ask:** see review's sentence-by-sentence account. A scoped run stops after its task and starts a Periodical only when the human's goal asks for one. Mint routes and UI are unchanged. General-run ranks are byte-identical. The PR names all four retirements.

**Changes I made after approval:** none. Review asked for no fixes and named no area-note entries.

### Ledger
1. **Inside: real scoped runs stop minting.** Settled by the deployed-code checks below. The rest is on review's named monitor and rollback.
   - *On what landed:* the live `GET /autopilot/kickoff` general render equals a local render at `b5950f704`, differing only in the per-request session UUID. Against base `da5df70` it differs in exactly review's three hunks: the manual sentence, the deleted tail paragraph, and step 5's stop.
   - *Scoped renders from the deployed code:* 12 renders cover ordinary, gate-marked Periodical review, and goal-asks-for-Periodical tasks, each in standard/stepper × write/readonly. All carry "start no Periodical unless the human's goal asks for". None carry the retired tail or review-marker wording. The goal case still renders the goal and the mint instruction.
   - *Live dispatches:* from the deploy to 22:44 UTC there were no `kind: periodical` dispatches. Baseline for the comparison: on 11 Nov, `Onboarding & Cold-Start Review + Autopilot` (21:19, minted with an operator note) and a plain `Test Coverage Gap Review` mint (21:57, origin not attributable from the dispatch list).
   - **Named monitor (review's):** compare `POST /api/proxy/periodicals/:id/mint` events before and after this deploy, correlated with the dispatching session and goal. A mint from a scoped Autopilot run whose goal asks for no Periodical is a failure. Expected: intentional mints only, and daily Periodical spend falls from about $101 (10 Nov). **Caveat for the reader:** scoped runs dispatched *before* the deploy still carry the old kickoff with the tail. These include this ticket's own Autopilot and LIN-4418's. If one of them mints at its finish, that is not a failure of this change. Count from runs dispatched after `b5950f7` went live.
   - **Named rollback (review's):** revert PR #2396's merge commit `b5950f704` on main. The change has no persisted data.
2. **Inside: a real Mint + Autopilot handoff chains no second mint.** **Not run.**
